newsitem.title: HONG KONG: S&P assigns new ratings to six Singapore banks.
newsitem.headline: S&P assigns new ratings to six Singapore banks.

text.p: Standard and Poor's Corp said on Monday it has assigned public information ratings to six Singapore banks.
The new ratings employ analytical procedures that parallel traditional credit ratings, but differ in that they are based on public disclosure and other sources of information, S&P said.
Singapore banks are the strongest in Asia, S&P said.
The rating agency said Singapore's banking system will continue to be the least risky, the strongest capitalised and one of the most profitable in Asia.
The domestic banks will become larger and stronger, in line with worldwide trends towards megabanks, S&P said.
The six locally incorporated banks also benefit from competitive restrictions on foreign banks in the domestic retail market , it said.
S&P also said that, subject to central bank approval, there are no major restrictions on Singapore banks' geographic representation or business activities.

This allows the banks to diversify their activities and promote new growth opportunities by expanding into non-bank financial services and into the developing countries in the Asia-Pacific region, it said.
